messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: routing latency alert — p99 router latency > 1.2s in eu-west-1 (nodes: router-eu-1a,e). Auto-escalation triggered. Paging oncall.
Alex P: I'm oncall, grabbing first-pass. Which tenants impacted? any customer-facing pages yet?
Maria G: I'm with Alex. Pulled the graphs — p95 ~ 320ms (ok), p99 jumped to ~1.25s in the last 7m. Streaming stalls visible on some sessions (clients see stalled tokens). Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/routers/router-latency?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west-1
Sam T: I see an abnormal amount of 502s from lb-edge1 -> router-eu-1a. Logs show a lot of reassigns and `route_decision: fallback` churn.
Devon L: Looking at routing table diffs, there's a recent policy rollout (policy-id: rollout-2026-03-15-1247) that introduced a new tie-breaker for hotkeys. Might be causing uneven shard weights. Pulling rbctl state now.
Alex P: Jia, can you check infra autoscaling/instance counts in eu-west-1? Could be we hit hot partitions and the pool didn't scale quickly.
Jia R: autoscaling groups healthy, no scale events. Instance CPU ~35% average. Not a capacity shortage overall.
Maria G: Ok, that leans towards misrouting/hot-partitioning rather than pure capacity. Sam, paste the LB -> router trace for a representative request.
Sam T: ```
[2026-03-15T12:47:01Z] client=10.4.2.11 -> lb-edge1 -> router-eu-1a
route_decision: hashed-shard=shard-107 -> assigned-node=router-eu-1c
followup: node-unavailable -> fallback-route=router-eu-1a
kv_cache_miss: tenant=acme-corp key=usr:session:abc123
latency: 1234ms
``` 
Sam T: There's a pattern: many requests get hashed to shard-107 but the node assigned is flapping between *healthy* router-eu-1c and router-eu-1a (which is getting overloaded). "fallback-route" seems to push traffic to a node that's already hot.
Devon L: That matches the new tie-breaker behavior — when shard weight is ambiguous we prefer same-az fallback; in regions with skewed shard ownership this can concentrate traffic. Looks like a policy bug in rollout-2026-03-15-1247.
incident-bot: Noted: rollout-2026-03-15-1247 is in canary -> 62% of traffic. Recommend rollback to previous policy version if confirmed.
Alex P: Action plan: 1) Pause policy rollout or revert, 2) Apply manual routing override for the hot tenant(s) to distribute across nodes, 3) Monitor p99 and streaming stalls, 4) Inform customers and runbook owners. Who takes rollback?
Maria G: I'll initiate a rollback of the routing policy to rollout-2026-03-14-1810. Sam, can you prepare the rollback command and dry-run output?
Sam T: Rollback dry-run: `rbctl rollback rollout-2026-03-15-1247 --to rollout-2026-03-14-1810 --dry-run` -> predicted affected shards: 120 (10 tenants). No config conflicts.
Sam T: Applying rollback now (non-dry-run): `rbctl rollback rollout-2026-03-15-1247 --to rollout-2026-03-14-1810`
incident-bot: Rollback started. Notifying canary monitors.
Alex P: While rollback proceeds, I'm applying a temporary per-tenant override for the top offending tenant (acme-corp) to spread its hotkey shards across two nodes. Command: `rbctl override --tenant acme-corp --shard-pattern usr:* --strategy spread --zones 2` — executing.
Devon L: Override applied. Also toggled `eager_fallback=false` for router-eu-1a to reduce forced fallbacks to that node.
Jia R: No infra actions needed. Autoscaling still stable. Network health looks fine.
Maria G: Visible improvement within ~90s of rollback + override. p99 dropped from 1.25s -> ~380ms. Streaming stall count down from 28 -> 3 in the last 5 minutes.
Support-Bot: Customer impact: 12 support tickets flagged under priority-high, top ticket: #3452 (Acme Corp) reporting streaming stalls during generation sessions. CS alerted and posting templated notice.
Alex P: Good. Can we validate tail latencies across all regions? Want to ensure no regression elsewhere.
Sam T: Quick sweep: us-west p99 stable, eu-west now trending down, ap-south unaffected. No cross-region fallout.
Maria G: Moving to monitoring window. We'll keep the thread open for 30m. Postmortem owners: Alex P (lead), Maria G (routing analysis), Sam T (LB/logs).
Devon L: Root cause hypothesis: bug in new tie-breaker logic in rollout-2026-03-15-1247 that biased fallback choices toward a single overloaded node under hot-key hash collisions -> hot partitioning -> tail latency spike and streaming stalls.
Alex P: Customer comms: @support please send interim notice to affected customers (apology + mitigations applied). CC: Enterprise accounts team.
Support-Bot: Sent interim notice to affected accounts list and created update in #customer-notifications.
Maria G: Logging runbook step: capture router debug dump (saved to s3://redwood-incidents/1781234567/) and snapshot routing table for postmortem. ```
rbctl dump-routing --region eu-west-1 > /tmp/routing-dump-1781234567.json
aws s3 cp /tmp/routing-dump-1781234567.json s3://redwood-incidents/1781234567/
```
Alex P: Great work. If p99 stays <500ms for 15m and streaming stalls remain <=5, we'll mark incident mitigated and start RCA. Next steps: full postmortem, rollback testing, add canary guardrail for tie-breaker rollouts.
Sam T: Confirmed 15m stability window reached. p99=340ms, streaming stalls=2.
incident-bot: Incident status changed to MITIGATED by Maria G at 2026-03-15T13:12:10Z
Alex P: Marking this thread for postmortem. Assigning timeline, logs, and owners. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:"
